decisions.title: Claude Design (Anthropic-native design engine) — candidate to replace Google Stitch in /bx:webdesign once it ships an API/MCP
decisions.note: User-directed registration after this session's research (finding is NOT from the changelog/docs/community lanes — Claude Design is a separate Anthropic Labs product, launched 2026-04-17, Opus-powered). Strong long-term fit for the /bx:webdesign design engine: same vendor as the harness, codebase-aware design-system extraction (maps onto Phase 1), exports standalone HTML. BLOCKED today: Claude Design is interactive web-only with NO API/MCP/CLI, so the headless MCP-driven skill (generate_screen_from_text / get_screen / edit_screens, screen IDs persisted in state.json) has nothing to call — a swap is impossible now, not just inadvisable. Related v2 question worth a brainstorm: whether Opus-native restyle generation removes the need for ANY external design engine (Stitch or Claude Design) at all.

decisions.title: Skills-directory plugins (`<name>@skills-dir`) auto-load with no marketplace/cache — could close the activation gap (docs + v2.1.178)
decisions.note: STRONGEST evidence yet for Next-Steps #1. A folder with `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` under `~/.claude/skills/` loads as `<name>@skills-dir` next session, discovered in place (not copied to the plugin cache) — personal-scope loads in every project with no install/update step, closing the plugin-cache-staleness/activation gap outright. Caveats: SKILL.md edits apply live but hooks/.mcp.json/agents/output-styles changes still need /reload-plugins; project-scope @skills-dir plugins don't walk up to repo root (launch from root). Cross-lane consolidated: docs plugins-reference (primary) corroborated by changelog v2.1.178 (nested .claude/skills contextual auto-load). Distinct-source companion to open findings 19758d30 (v2.1.157) + 0e4083ea (/reload-skills) under this same pain slug. Evaluate converting bx from marketplace→skills-dir; if adopted, update the S37 'Plugin approach' decision + README install steps. ADDENDUM 2026-07-22: the docs lane re-emitted this same finding_id from a DIFFERENT section of the same page — 'Version management', which states '/plugin update or auto-update fires' and confirms bx's omitted-`version` field means commit-SHA versioning ('users get updates on every new commit'). Implies an automatic update path may already exist alongside the manual step; the fetched section does not specify the auto-update trigger cadence or scope, so verify live behavior before softening the manual `/plugin update bx` + `/reload-plugins` instructions in README.md / workflow.md / fix-mode-evolve.md. stored source_content_hash intentionally left anchored to the original skills-dir excerpt (open entries have no hash-trigger semantics; Rules 3/5 cover rejected/deferred only).

The launcher is verified working since S39 and /bx:seo has still never had a real run — do not touch the dispatch path before that run.

decisions.title: Docs document only `Agent(<subagent-name>)` deny rules — the `Agent(model:opus)` tip applied 2026-07-05 is uncorroborated by the sub-agents/settings pages
decisions.note: APPLIED 2026-07-22, but the lane's PREMISE WAS WRONG — resolved by orchestrator verification against https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions#match-by-input-parameter (outside the docs lane's pinned allowlist, which is why the lane missed it). `Agent(model:opus)` IS real and documented under 'Match by input parameter'; the v2.1.178-sourced tip applied in finding 2d6b0e5f was NOT wrong about the syntax. The finding survived for a different and more serious reason: the same docs section states 'a parameter the model omits is never matched', and the S43 bug was a GENERIC subagent dispatched with no `model` param at all — so the deny rule would never have fired on the exact bug the tip claimed to guard. Rewrote workflow.md's 'Guarding subagent model routing' section: 'permission-layer backstop' → 'partial permission-layer backstop', and replaced the 'Belt-and-suspenders … stops a regression from ever spawning a non-Sonnet bx agent' overclaim with the omitted-parameter limit + two further caveats (literal-input comparison before normalization, so alias `opus` matches but a full model ID does not; parameter rules valid in deny/ask only, never allow) and a pointer back to frontmatter `model:` + dispatch-by-name as the durable guard. LESSON for scan-docs.md: the pinned allowlist lacks the permissions page, which owns permission-rule syntax — consider adding it. Orchestrator normalized the lane's `bx:*/agent-model-deny-rule-syntax` to `bx:agents/...` per the bx:<skill>/<area> capability-string form.

decisions.title: Official Code Review runs a dedicated false-positive verification step; /bx:review has none
decisions.note: PARTIALLY APPLIED 2026-07-30 -- READ THIS BEFORE ASSUMING THE GAP IS CLOSED. Only the cheap 'verification bar' half landed: bx/skills/review/references/output-format.md gained Rule 8 requiring Critical/Important findings to name a concrete failure scenario (input/state/call sequence producing the wrong behaviour) cited to file:line rather than inferred from naming, downgrading to Suggestion otherwise -- mirroring the REVIEW.md verification-bar pattern in Anthropic's Code Review docs. DELIBERATELY NOT DONE: the actual architectural fix, i.e. the dedicated verification/refutation PASS that filters candidate findings against real code behaviour before they are presented. /bx:review remains a single-orchestrator, single-pass skill with no independent verification stage, and that compounds with its effort: high setting (see finding 069c9442). Applying a multi-agent topology through a --fix diff gate was rejected as unsafe for a skill that has never had a skill-creator content review or an eval suite. NEXT: brainstorm -> spec -> plan, then measure with skill-creator's eval loop; re-register as a fresh finding if a future run re-emits the capability.

decisions.title: `ReportFindings` tool (v2.1.218) renders findings as a host-native list — /bx:review emits markdown tables only
decisions.note: SCOPED RUN (review-only). ORCHESTRATOR-VERIFIED. references/output-format.md specifies a hand-rolled markdown severity table; the host can render a typed findings list instead when it requests one. Note the official severity taxonomy (Important / Nit / Pre-existing) differs from bx:review's (Critical / Important / Suggestions / Convention Violations) — 'Pre-existing' has no bx equivalent though SKILL.md Step 0 covers the concept in prose. Evaluate adopting ReportFindings and whether to add a pre-existing marker.

decisions.title: `effort: high` widens the net and admits lower-confidence findings per official calibration — undocumented tradeoff in /bx:review
decisions.note: APPLIED 2026-07-30. bx/skills/review/SKILL.md: added a 'Why effort: high, and what it costs' callout after the Fresh-session tip. States Anthropic's documented tradeoff (low/medium report only high-confidence findings; high through max cast a wider net and admit less certain ones), explicitly flags that whether a skill's effort: frontmatter inherits that exact calibration is NOT documented, and routes the user to --verify as the existing mitigation. The effort value itself was deliberately NOT changed -- high is correct for the thorough tier; the gap was that the cost went unstated.

STILL UNVERIFIED: /loop (ScheduleWakeup, session-scoped) and /schedule are different mechanisms; smoke-test and replace the hedge with a definitive statement.

Use Esc Esc or /rewind to undo'). Model correction to copy: review/SKILL.md:145. Grep false positives excluded: seo/SKILL.md:522, save/references/mode-update.md:362 (unrelated 'individually'). decisions.title: code-review docs state the disable-model-invocation scheduled-prompt caveat as plain fact — firm up workflow.md's /loop hedge from 'speculative' to 'documented for the mechanism class'
decisions.note: APPLIED 2026-08-11: workflow.md caveat retitled 'Partially confirmed' and now quotes the docs sentence verbatim — documented behavior for /schedule-style scheduled tasks; the /loop-specific half stays hedged and the smoke-test task remains open.
